text.p: United States Surgical Corp., turning on the heat in its $230 million hostile takeover bid for Circon Corp., said Tuesday it has filed a lawsuit to force Circon to drop its recently adopted "poison pill" takeover defence and "golden parachute" executive compensation plans.
Circon declined to comment until it had been served notice of the lawsuit.
U.S. Surgical also said it will soon file another suit to force Circon to disclose information that the surgical products company needs to communicate directly with Circon's shareholders.
U.S. Surgical said Circon has so far refused to provide the information it says it is entitled to under Delaware law.

Circon, a supplier of products for minimally invasive surgery, already faces three lawsuits by shareholders for rejecting U.S. Surgical's cash offer of $18 a share, or $230 million, which was made on Aug. 2.

U.S. Surgical filed the suit in the Delaware Chancery Court, claiming that Circon's board of directors breached fiduciary duties by taking steps for the "improper sole purpose of cementing Circon President and CEO Richard Auhll's continuing control over the company."

On Aug. 27, Circon offered 300 key employees special incentives to remain with the company, and unspecified severance benefits payable upon involuntary termination of employment if the company changed hands.
Santa Barbara, Calif.-based Circon also recently adopted a shareholder rights plan to thwart unwanted takeover attempts.
Norwalk, Conn.-based U.S. Surgical said Circon's stated desire to protect benefits of last year's purchase of Cabot Medical Corp. did not justify the "poison pill."
Nevertheless, U.S. Surgical said that nearly 7 million Circon shares had been tendered as of Aug. 29. This is about 76 percent of the stock not owned by Circon's management and board, it said.
U.S. Surgical, one of the world's largest makers of minimally invasive surgical products, said it would continue to pursue a merger with Circon.
U.S. Surgical's stock fell 12.5 cents to $38.875 on the New York Stock Exchange, and Circon also lost 12.5 cents to $18.125 on Nasdaq.
